reader.requirement: At --std 85 a sort-merge file description entry must begin with the level indicator SD immediately followed by file-name-1; an entry with the name before SD, with SD and no file-name, or with no level indicator must be refused, and SD file-name-1 with or without the RECORD and DATA RECORDS clauses must be accepted.
reader.edition-search: The grammar rule `sortMergeDescriptionEntry : SD fileName sortMergeDescriptionClauses? DOT dataDescriptionEntry*` carries no semantic predicate; ClosedFormatPass reports at every edition (its summary: error at every edition and every strictness); grep of ClosedFormatPass.cs for Edition/Version/Std finds only the EditionContext used for positions. The DATA RECORDS removal gate (COBOL0873 at 2023) is another rule's edition arm.
reader.behaviour-differs-by-edition: no (for SR1); the DATA RECORDS clause the 1985 entry also admits is accepted at 85 and refused COBOL0873 at 2023, a different rule

refuter.evidence: Read §1985:XI.3.2.2/3.2.3 and the Data Division summary format (SD file-name-1 RECORD.. DATA RECORDS only; no GLOBAL/EXTERNAL/LABEL in the 1985 SD). Probes at --std 85 under E:/COBOL-coord/scratch/coderead-1985/out/refute-1985-070/: r1glob 'SD SF IS GLOBAL.' and r1glob2 'SD SF GLOBAL.' -> COBOL1970 (refused; 1985 SD has no GLOBAL); r1ext 'SD SF IS EXTERNAL.' -> COBOL1970; r1label 'SD SF LABEL RECORDS ARE STANDARD.' -> COBOL1970; r1order 'SD SF DATA RECORD IS SREC RECORD CONTAINS 4 CHARACTERS.' compiles and runs AAAA (SR2 order immaterial); r1nodot (no terminating period) -> COBOL0307/COBOL1970. With the reader's misorder/no-name/no-indicator refusals, SR1 holds. cite.py: OK §1985:XI.3.2.3 SR1 the text is in SR1.
